title: Mary, Help of Christians (24 May)
hookLine: a title loved by John Bosco and Australian Catholics

cards: A wedding in Cana. The party is in full swing, and somewhere near the kitchen the wine has just run out, in front of every guest. The couple may not know yet.
But one guest does. She doesn't make a scene. She walks over to her son and says four plain words.
No speech, no plan, just the problem, handed to the one who can do something about it. Today, a title Catholics give that guest: Mary, Help of Christians.

teach.b: Here's what she says, in the Douay-Rheims: "They have no wine."

teach.h: SHE NOTICES, ASKS, POINTS TO HIM.
teach.b: She notices a need before anyone asks, and she brings it to Jesus. Then she turns to the servants: "Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye." Catholics see in this scene the whole shape of Mary's help.
She notices. She brings the need to her son. And she points people back to him.
Help of Christians is one of the titles Catholics call her by in the Litany of Loreto, a long prayer of names for Mary, each followed by the words pray for us.

The title has been prayed in hard times: by people under threat, by people in exile, by a Church in trouble. Tradition ties it to moments when Catholics believed her prayers had helped them through danger.
Then there's John Bosco, the Italian priest who gave his life to poor and abandoned boys in Turin.
He loved this title, built a church in Turin under it, and, tradition says, credited Mary, Help of Christians, with what his work achieved. His followers carried the devotion far beyond Turin.
In Australia, Catholics honor Mary under this title as the patron of their country.

teach.h: WHATSOEVER HE SHALL SAY TO YOU, DO YE.
teach.b: Catholics and other Christians differ on how to speak of Mary. Catholics, like Orthodox Christians, ask for her prayers, while Protestant churches generally address prayer to God alone.
For Catholics, her help is never separate from Christ. It's what she did at Cana: noticing, asking him, and saying, do what he tells you.

how: Catholics invoke Mary as Help of Christians in the Litany of Loreto; the Salesians of John Bosco and the Church in Australia keep 24 May as a special feast, and the invocation 'Mary, Help of Christians, pray for us' is a common short prayer.

practice: Bring to mind something that has run out, patience at home, money at the end of the month, hope for someone you love, and say it as plainly as Mary did: they have no wine; I have no patience; she has no hope.
If you pray, use the line from the litany, Help of Christians, pray for us; if you don't, simply name what's empty and sit with it honestly, without dressing it up.

wordCard.voice: Mary. Under the title Help of Christians: the one who noticed the wine was gone at Cana, and told the servants to do what her son said.

orig.note: Latin: help of Christians — the title as it stands in the Litany of Loreto.

carryVoice: Your line: help of Christians. At Cana, her help pointed straight to her son. Day nine hundred ninety-five, done.
